Radiology Division | Amsterdam UMC (AMC site) | 05 January 2025
Exam: Multiparametric MRI of the prostate

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation for suspected prostate cancer. PSA 12.87 ng/mL with prior biopsy bucket "Positive".

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 52.0 mL in total volume. T2-weighted sequences highlight a 18 mm focal hypointense area situated in the right anterior mid-gland. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction, mirrored by low ADC signal. Dynamic contrast studies capture early, focal enhancement in that exact region. Extracapsular spread and seminal vesicle involvement are absent. Pelvic lymph nodes appear normal. Skeletal survey reveals no suspicious bone lesions.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right anterior mid-gland.
Prostate volume 52.0 mL; PSA density 0.25 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.85843223.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Routine cardiovascular risk screening flagged a PSA reading of 8.2 ng/mL. The gentleman noted mild urinary hesitancy, though acute retention was absent. Concurrent thyroid panels were drawn.

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Subsequent testing showed the PSA climbing to 11.0 ng/mL. Lower urinary tract symptoms persist at a moderate level, scoring 17 on the IPSS. Earlier transperineal sampling established Gleason 4+3, ISUP GG 3 disease. Ongoing monitoring continues without intervention.
